newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close firmer in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close firmer in quiet session.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed firmer in quiet trade on Wednesday, but ended the day off earlier highs after some stronger than expected U.S. economic data, analysts said.

"We had a stronger U.S. dollar and that helped the U.S. market and by extension the Canadian market when we opened up," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada. "All of that was erased at 10 o'clock when we got evidence of stronger growth in the U.S."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.15 to C$115.80 to yield 6.716 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bonds rose 6/32 to yield 6.43 percent. The spread between the two was 29 basis points, unchanged from Tuesday's close.

Canadian bonds opened stronger this morning amid some buying by Japanese accounts and market friendly data in the United States and Canada. Canadian data included a report that industrial product prices fell in October.
Canadian bonds later pared gains after reports that U.S. durable goods rose a higher than expected 0.1 percent and the November Chicago Purchasing Managers index also rose.

Trading volumes in the Canadian market were lower than usual this afternoon amid a recommended early close in the U.S. bond market ahead of Thursday's U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday. While the Canadian bond market will remain open Thursday, trading was expected to be listless in the absence of U.S. action.

In auction news, the Government of Canada sold C$400 million in 30-year 4.25 percent real return bonds. The auction produced a high yield of 3.980 percent. Bids from primary dealers totaled C$985 million, including C$27 million non-competitive tenders at the allotment yield.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.24 to C$106.97 to yield 6.060 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 3/32 to yield 6.12 percent.
The negative spread between the two widened to six from five basis points at Tuesday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.73 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.15 percent.
